questions.q: What does a Task's WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA(...) clause accomplish?
options: The Task's warehouse only wakes up and the MERGE only runs when the Stream actually has unconsumed data
It forces the Task to run every second regardless of data
It deletes the Stream after each run
It prevents the Task from ever being suspended
questions.explain: The WHEN clause is the efficiency gate — on a quiet day with no new data, the scheduled tick does nothing and nothing gets billed.

questions.q: Why is ticket_facts_sync_task's MERGE described as idempotent?
options: It never actually writes any data
It has no WHEN MATCHED branch at all
Its UPDATE SET branch sets columns to the same value whether it runs once or twice against the same change rows
It only runs one time ever, by Snowflake design
questions.explain: An upsert MERGE with an UPDATE branch produces the same end state whether it processes the same rows once or twice.

questions.q: Why does finance_refund_task's MERGE have no WHEN MATCHED branch?
options: Snowflake does not allow WHEN MATCHED in any MERGE statement
refund_events is append-only by design — each row is a distinct refund event, not a value to overwrite in place
It was left out by mistake and should be added
WHEN MATCHED is only valid for VARIANT columns
questions.explain: refund_events logs discrete refund events; only WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT fits that append-only design.

questions.q: What state is a newly created Task in by default, before anyone resumes it?
options: SUSPENDED
RUNNING
DELETED
FAILED
questions.explain: Tasks are created suspended as a deliberate safety default — Lesson 7 resumes them explicitly.

questions.q: What real risk does this lesson flag about finance_refund_task's append-only MERGE, specifically?
options: It would silently skip all refund rows with a null refund_amount
It cannot reference a VARIANT column in its USING clause
If the same stream rows were somehow fed into it twice in overlapping windows, both runs could each insert a matching event, duplicating the ledger
It would fail to compile because it lacks a WHEN MATCHED branch
questions.explain: Because the MERGE is not idempotent, duplicate or overlapping processing of the same Stream data can produce duplicate ledger rows — exactly the mechanism behind this chapter's later bug.
